title: The Stone Where All Readings Rest Forever

features.name: the reading stone
features.desc-on-touch: A ledger carved into bedrock, its surface worn smooth by fingers that stopped coming. Every word is still legible if you know how stone reads.

features.name: the sediment pages
features.desc-on-touch: Paper has become layer. Each stratum holds a reading, and the readings have fused together until no single page can be lifted without taking them all.

features.name: the light that teaches geology
features.desc-on-touch: A shaft of light falls through a crack, touching the stone at one point that changes with the slow years. It is annotating the rock.

features.name: the fossils of ink
features.desc-on-touch: Shells and spirals have preserved written words. The animals died making the very mineral that would hold letters for ten thousand years.

features.name: the archive desk of stone
features.desc-on-touch: A desk where readings were catalogued, now carved into the bedrock itself. The drawers are fossils. The ink is iron oxide.

features.name: the root that learned mineral
features.desc-on-touch: A root has grown into the stone and is becoming stone. It remembers water and is forgetting it. In a few centuries it will be indistinguishable from the rock.

inscription: nothing is lost here, everything is consolidated

reverie.title: REVERIE — tide-pool at noon
narr: You're both holding stones worn smooth, picked from
the tidal line. She reads the fossil in it, a spiral
that lived two hundred million years before anyone
invented reading. You watch the light cross her face—
thinking the stone was a book, thinking the book
was a stone, neither of you asking which was true.

exits.label: back up toward the seabed where readings still move
deeper into the understory where stone dreams of being alive again
